oewn-00799906-n.learner: a set of actions that people carry out to support an idea or to reach a particular goal
examples: She gave many years of her life to the cause of clean water for every village.

oewn-01185144-n.learner: any case in a court of law in which a person asks the court for a remedy under the law
examples: The judge heard the widow's cause and ruled in her favour.

oewn-01027620-n.learner: in a court case, a step in which one side says that a question, a witness, a piece of evidence, or some other matter is not proper and should stop, and asks the court to decide whether it is improper or against the law
examples: The lawyer raised an objection to the question, and the judge agreed with her.

oewn-13736289-n.learner: a unit for measuring temperature on a particular scale
examples: Water boils at one hundred degrees on the Celsius scale.

oewn-13632450-n.learner: a unit for measuring arcs and angles
examples: A right angle measures ninety degrees.

oewn-05101827-n.learner: how serious something is, such as a burn or a crime
examples: He was found guilty of murder in the first degree.

oewn-05869901-n.learner: in maths, the highest power to which a term or variable is raised
examples: The equation x squared plus three x equals zero has a degree of two.

oewn-01844678-v.learner: to travel on a plane, a bus, or some other vehicle
examples: She hopped a bus into town to see her friend.

oewn-02099200-v.learner: to jump from one side of something to the other
examples: The boy hopped the little stream without getting his feet wet.

oewn-02099338-v.learner: to cross a place or a great distance as if it were only a short plane trip
examples: They hopped the Atlantic for a weekend in London.

oewn-13366301-n.learner: a British word for some kinds of insurance
examples: He took out life assurance to protect his family.

oewn-00065410-v.learner: to go through something such as an injury or an illness
examples: He suffered a broken leg when he fell from the ladder.

oewn-02114536-v.learner: to go through something, or meet with it, as it happens to you
examples: The little ship suffered a terrible fate in the storm.

oewn-00205234-v.learner: to be put in a weaker or worse position
examples: Honest traders suffered because the cheats could sell at lower prices.
His work began to suffer when he stopped sleeping well.

oewn-02725682-v.learner: to have a habit of something or a tendency toward it
examples: He suffers from a tendency to talk too much at dinner.

oewn-01770600-v.learner: to be concerned with something, so that you worry about it
examples: He cares too much about his weight and checks it every morning.

oewn-02441196-v.learner: to be in charge of something, to take action on it, or to deal with it and get it finished
examples: Who will care for the accounts while she is away?

oewn-01843112-v.learner: to go to or toward a place or thing
examples: When the wind rose, the little boat turned and sought the harbour.

oewn-01072011-v.learner: to ask someone for something, such as information
examples: We were lost, so we sought directions from a man at the station.

oewn-02625504-v.learner: to stay at someone's home as their guest
examples: Every summer we visit my aunt for two weeks.

oewn-01847990-v.learner: to come to see a person or place as part of your job or official duty
examples: An inspector visited the school to check the classrooms.

oewn-01040538-v.learner: to talk with someone in a friendly way without sharing much real information
examples: We sat on the porch and visited for an hour.

oewn-00750288-v.learner: to make something unpleasant fall on someone
examples: He feared that his crimes would be visited on his children.
That winter the town was visited by a terrible fever.

oewn-14517010-n.learner: the state of being extremely poor
examples: Many families lived in want during the long, hard winter.
